issues.description: Field Farm.animals: The problem statement (UML and textual instructions) requires Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> and explicitly asks to implement it using an ArrayList initialized in the no-argument constructor. The solution implementation declares private Set<Animal> animals and initializes it with new HashSet<>(), and its getter/setter use Set<Animal>. This mismatch changes collection type, ordering guarantees, and duplicate semantics and therefore conflicts with the specification and template instructions, confusing students and potentially causing tests expecting a List to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement. Recommended: modify the solution to declare 'private List<Animal> animals;', import java.util.List and java.util.ArrayList, initialize the field in the no-arg constructor with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();', and update the getter/setter signatures to return/accept List<Animal>. Ensure singFarmSong() and feedAllAnimals() iterate over the List. Alternatively, if a Set is intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify Set/HashSet and document the change in ordering/duplicate behavior.

issues.description: The Farm class' animals collection is described in the problem statement as a List (specifically an ArrayList) named 'animals', and the textual task explicitly instructs to "Initialize the ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments." In the solution implementation the same conceptual element is declared as a Set named 'animals' and initialized with new HashSet<>(), creating an inconsistency: problem statement expects a List/ArrayList (animals: List<Animal> / ArrayList initialization), while the solution uses Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>(). A student reading the instructions and the solution/template will be uncertain which collection type to implement, and this mismatch could block or confuse them when they must match the tests or follow the explicit instruction to use an ArrayList.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent. Preferred fix to match the problem statement: in solution (and template guidance) change the Farm class to declare the attribute as 'private List<Animal> animals;' and initialize it in the no-argument constructor with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();'. Update the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if using a Set is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to state 'Set/HashSet' instead of 'List/ArrayList' and remove the explicit instruction to initialize an ArrayList so students are not required to use a List.
